title: The Mess That We Made
author: Michelle Lord
intro: Some children in a little boat discover a huge mess of rubbish in the ocean.
checkedAgainst: Storyline Online page and teacher guide

questions.q: Who is in the little boat?
questions.clue: They are young people, sitting in a small boat.
questions.yes: A group of children is in the little boat.

questions.q: Where is the little boat floating?

options.text: In the middle of the ocean

questions.clue: It is a very big body of salty water.
questions.yes: The little boat is floating in the ocean.

questions.q: What is the mess floating in the water?
questions.clue: It is things that people have thrown away.
questions.yes: Plastic and rubbish are floating in the water.

questions.q: Which animals are mentioned first swimming in the mess?
questions.clue: Seals like to eat these swimming creatures.
questions.yes: Fish swim in the mess that we made.

questions.q: What happens to the seal in the story?

options.text: It gets caught in a net
It goes to sleep on rocks
It swims into a dark cave

questions.clue: Something dropped from a fishing boat traps the seal.
questions.yes: The seal gets caught in a fishing net.

questions.q: Where does the net come from?

options.text: A wooden pier by the shore

questions.clue: It comes from a big metal boat on the water.
questions.yes: The net comes from a boat of welded steel.

questions.q: Why does the turtle get trapped?
questions.clue: Rubbish from the landfill spills into the sea and traps it.
questions.yes: The turtle gets trapped in plastic that was thrown away.

questions.q: Where does the plastic spill from before entering the sea?
questions.clue: It is a place on land piled high with rubbish.
questions.yes: The plastic spills from a landfill that grows each day.

questions.q: Why is the landfill growing each day?
questions.clue: People at work and at play throw things into it.
questions.yes: People at work and at play stuff the landfill each day.

questions.q: How do the children feel when they see the huge mess?
questions.clue: Seeing the dirty ocean and trapped animals makes them sad and worried.
questions.yes: The children feel upset when they see all the rubbish.

questions.q: Who does the story say can save the day?
questions.clue: The people who made the mess can also fix it.
questions.yes: We are the ones who can save the day.

questions.q: Where do the children go to join a clean-up?
questions.clue: It is the sandy land right next to the sea.
questions.yes: The children reach a beach where people are cleaning up.

questions.q: What do the children do to help the animals?

options.text: Rescue the turtle and free the seal
Build a big tank for the fish
Feed bread to the hungry seagulls

questions.clue: They collect the nets and help the trapped sea creatures.
questions.yes: They rescue the turtle, collect the nets, and free the seal.

questions.q: Why do people clean up and reduce waste?
questions.clue: They want the sea to be clean and safe for marine life.
questions.yes: People work together to save the ocean.

questions.q: How do the sea animals feel after the ocean is cleaned?
questions.clue: The nets and plastic are gone, so they can swim safely.
questions.yes: The sea animals live happily in the clean ocean.
